issue.title: Upgrade Python on win2 and test whether the access violations stop

labels.name: win2
labels.description: Task for win2, the Windows desktop

issue.body:
**What.** Upgrade Python on win2 and test whether the access violations stop (Nathan, 2026-11-08).
- Install the newest Python 3.14.x beside 3.12. Do not remove 3.12, and do not touch #82's running processes, which keep their 3.12 venv until #82 ends.
- Make a new venv on 3.14 with python-flint 0.9.0 pinned (the same FLINT 3.6.0 as the other machines), mpmath 1.3.0, sympy, numpy and scipy. Rebuild hp's kernel for it (`hp/build.sh`, local machine) if a task needs hp.
- Run a crash test on the new venv: #146's repeat-and-compare loop, the amplitude copy `amp_flint_par.py 1.10 15 750 640 --procs 1 --fit phys --mf 6:12`, for at least 24 h beside #82. After #82 ends, run it under full load.

- **CPU temperatures (Nathan, 2026-11-08).** Within a minute of every crash of any process (Application log event 1000, or a WER report), record the CPU package and per-core temperatures, the clocks if available, and the load. Add the same reading to the 5-minute cpu and memory log as the baseline, so a crash's reading can be set against it. Use a built-in source first, such as the ACPI thermal zone over WMI or the CPU's own sensors through PowerShell. If none gives the CPU's temperature, report that and ask before installing a monitoring tool. Tools that read the sensors usually load a kernel driver.

**Why.** win2 had four python.exe access violations (0xc0000005) in 22 hours, each at a different offset:

| UTC | process | module |
|---|---|---|
| 11-07 18:37 | python | python312.dll |
| 11-08 07:00 | a #82 worker | libflint (python-flint) |
| 11-08 14:40 | a negative-mass job | python312.dll |
| 11-08 16:31 | a negative-mass job | python312.dll |

None repeated on a rerun, and #140 and #146 found no wrong result. Nathan's rule was no BIOS update unless win2 crashed again; it has, and he chose to try a Python upgrade first.

**Acceptance (can fail).**
- Every amplitude copy on 3.14 hashes to fd6b5ef2f90d4f559a1a1ab68a7e85fe7c9b8538cc7e50ac41d2fb5510eb47d8, the hash of macm3 and of win2's 3.12 copies (#161). A different hash names the first differing σ string.
- Record every crash of any process during the test from the Application log (event 1000, WER 1001): time, process, module, offset, code. Record the WHEA events too.
- Every crash has its temperature reading within a minute, set against the baseline's distribution (median and maximum under the same load).
- The verdict is reported against the rate before the upgrade, about one crash per 5.5 h under load. Zero crashes in 24 h has about a 1% chance at the old rate, so it counts as evidence the upgrade helped. A crash in python314.dll or libflint at a new random offset points to the hardware, not Python.

**Depends on.** Nothing for the install. The full-load phase waits for #82 to end.

Started, win2, 2026-11-08 16:43 UTC. Plan:
1. Python 3.14.10 (the newest 3.14.x on python.org, installer `python-3.14.10-amd64.exe`) installed for the user only, with no PATH change, no `py` launcher change and no file association, so 3.12 and every running job keep resolving as they do. 2. A new venv `venv-t177` on 3.14 with python-flint 0.9.0, mpmath 1.3.0, sympy, numpy and scipy; `pip freeze` and the FLINT version recorded.
3. A loop of rounds, each three `amp_flint_par.py 1.10 15 750 640 --procs 1 --fit phys --mf 6:12` copies in parallel (one thread each, Normal priority, `PYTHONFAULTHANDLER=1`), every JSON hashed with #140's `compare.py` against fd6b5ef2f90d4f559a1a1ab68a7e85fe7c9b8538cc7e50ac41d2fb5510eb47d8 and against each other, for at least 24 h; full load after #82 ends.
4. A watcher that polls the Application log every minute for a new event 1000 or WER 1001 from any process and WHEA events, and records each in `I177-win2/crashes.txt`. It kills nothing and changes no setting.
5. CPU temperatures: see the next comment; the built-in sources give no CPU temperature on this board, so I am asking before anything is installed.

Memory: the loop adds three single-process copies to #82's twelve processes; I will measure their working set and post it against the projection (free 12 to 15 GB at #82's peak, 20:40 to 21:20 UTC).

Install, venv, loop and watcher are up, 16:52 UTC. Details are in `I177-win2/install_record.txt`.

| item | value |

**Loop.** Started 2026-11-08 16:50:36 UTC: rounds of three `amp_flint_par.py 1.10 15 750 640 --procs 1 --fit phys --mf 6:12` copies in parallel (one thread each, Normal priority, `PYTHONFAULTHANDLER=1`), checkout `..\choptuik-i140` (d9fab0b), each JSON hashed with #140's `compare.py` against fd6b5ef2f90d4f559a1a1ab68a7e85fe7c9b8538cc7e50ac41d2fb5510eb47d8 (`compare_amp.py`; its `--selftest` passes: a clean round passes, and a changed digit, a missing JSON and a non-zero exit are each flagged; the reference JSON of #146 round 1 hashes to that value). The loop runs until a `STOP` file appears; the number of copies is read from `COPIES` at each round start, so I can raise it when #82 ends. The copies' working set is 0.3 GB each early in a run; I will post the peak.

**Crash watcher.** `crash_watch.py` polls the Application log every minute for event 1000 and 1002 of any process, a new WER report directory, and WHEA-Logger, Kernel-Power 41, BugCheck 1001 and 6008 in the System log. On the first one it writes `crashes.txt` and a reading to `crash_temps.txt` and wakes this session. It kills nothing. Backfill of the log (`crashes.txt`) holds the four python crashes of the issue's table with offsets and pids.

**CPU temperature: no built-in source, so I stop here and ask.** Source tried and result, read only and not elevated:

| source | result |
|---|---|
| `Thermal Zone Information` performance counters | the set exists, it has no instances (`The specified instance is not present`) |
| WMI `root/wmi` `MSAcpi_ThermalZoneTemperature` | `Not supported` |
| `Win32_TemperatureProbe` | empty |
| sensor tool or driver | none installed (the only matching driver is `intelpep`) |

The board is an ASRock Z890I Nova WiFi with an Intel Core Ultra 7 265K; its sensors are not exposed to Windows without a driver. Tools that read them (HWiNFO, LibreHardwareMonitor and the like) load a kernel driver, so I install none without Nathan's OK, and an elevated shell would not add a CPU zone to a board that exposes none. What I record instead, from built-in counters (`sensors.py`, `sensor_log.py` every 5 min into `sensor_log.txt` as the baseline, and at each crash into `crash_temps.txt`): the clock per thread (min, mean, max), `% Processor Performance`, `% Processor Utility`, and the package and cores power from the RAPL Energy Meter (read as milliwatts). ```

Coordinator: Nathan installed Core Temp on win2 (2026-11-08), and it is running. Its readings go into each crash record and the 5-minute log, read-only from its shared memory with no change to its settings. That settings point was the stop condition of the issue's temperature item, and it is now resolved.

CPU temperatures from Core Temp, 17:40 UTC. Source and first readings, as the coordinator asked (Nathan installed Core Temp on win2; it started at 17:35:00 UTC).

**Source.** Core Temp's shared-memory block `CoreTempMappingObjectEx`, opened read-only (`OpenFileMappingW` and `MapViewOfFile` with `FILE_MAP_READ` only, `I177-win2/coretemp.py`, standard library). Nothing in Core Temp is touched: no setting, no logging, no plug-in, no driver of mine. The layout is the struct on the developer page (https://alcpu.com/CoreTemp/developers.html). My first parse used a layout from memory that put the trailing arrays in a different order, so the CPU name and flags read empty; I replaced it with the page's layout before using any value (offsets 0 to 2576 were the same in both: loads, TjMax, core counts, temperatures, VID, speed). The mapping is a page-rounded 8192 bytes; `uiStructVersion` reads 2.

| field | value |
|---|---|
| CPU name | Intel Core Ultra 7 265K (Arrow Lake) |
| cores, CPUs | 20, 1 (one value per core) |
| TjMax | 105 °C |
| Fahrenheit flag, delta-to-TjMax flag | 0, 0 (the values are °C, not distance below TjMax) |
| VID, speed | 1.20 to 1.25 V, 5187 MHz |

**Plausibility** (14 samples, 5 s apart, 17:38 UTC, #82 and the I7 jobs and the loop running):
- All 280 values are between 56.5 and 94.5 °C, below TjMax 105. Raw values end in .5 (58.5, 72.5, ...), so they are steps of 1 °C offset by 0.5; I record them rounded to whole degrees.
- Between cores, the mean temperature follows the mean load (correlation 0.76 over 20 cores); within one core over time the correlation with its load is 0.30. The E-cores come in groups of four with equal values (72, 72, 72, 72), which fits a shared sensor per cluster. I cannot show the idle value, because the machine is busy.
- The Windows counter clock in my first log lines (3300/3540/3900 MHz) is the nominal frequency; Core Temp's 5187 MHz agrees with `% Processor Performance` of 128 to 136 on the 3.9 GHz base.

**First readings** (the 5-minute log, now with the Core Temp part, `sensor_log.txt`):

```
2026-11-08 17:39:34Z  util 105%  package 118.5 W  cores 108.6 W  | Core Temp: per-core C min/mean/max 62/73.9/78
                      [62,66,74,74,74,74,72,76,68,68,78,78,76,76,78,78,76,76,76,68]  TjMax 105  VID 1.241 V  5187 MHz
2026-11-08 17:38:04Z  util 83%   package 104.9 W  cores 95.0 W   | Core Temp: per-core C min/mean/max 58/69.6/80
14 samples from about 17:38 UTC, 5 s apart: highest single core 94.5 C, mean of the 20 cores 69.6 to 77.0 C
```

A crash is now recorded with the per-core temperatures, their maximum, TjMax and the CPU name: `crash_temps.txt` gets the same line format, read within about 35 s of the event (the watcher now polls every 30 s, was 60 s). The seven crashes before 17:39 have no temperature; the next one will. Core Temp must keep running for this: if it closes, the block disappears and the lines say `n/a (Core Temp: ...)`.

One observation, no conclusion: single cores reached 94.5 °C, 10 °C below TjMax, while the package drew 105 to 157 W. The CPU name, TjMax and the temperatures are Core Temp's; I have not checked them against another sensor.

**For the BIOS question, from the web (not from win2).** ASRock's BIOS page for this board, as summarized by the search tool (I could not open the page's list itself, it is script-rendered, so this needs checking by hand): 1.38 is listed as the first release, dated 2024-09-23 (win2 reports 2024-09-08, the build date), with no microcode note; later entries add Intel microcode 0x117 (2.26, 2025-03-28), 0x11A and an ME update (3.10, 2025-09-11), a microcode and ME update (3.14, 2026-01-06), and 0x121 (3.20, 2026-01-29), listed as the newest. The search also returned one forum post saying a BIOS with the "Intel 200S Boost" feature blocked XMP frequency changes on that user's board, one anecdote I did not check.
